phenotype_specificity.statement: 37342083: the proband was tested with a targeted autoinflammatory NGS panel; because of parental consanguinity, 14 genes for recessive autoinflammatory diseases were reported as negative. The authors describe the features as typical of HA20.

quotes.quote: To identify the molecular basis of the patients’ disease, targeted next-generation sequencing (NGS) for autoinflammatory diseases was conducted on a DNA sample from proband II.2.

Noteworthy, in this patient born to a consanguineous union, no mutation was found in the following genes known to be involved in autosomal recessive autoinflammatory diseases: ADA2, IL10, IL10RA, IL10RB, IL1RN, IL36RN, IL6ST, LACC1, LPIN2, MEFV, MVK, NLRP1, OTULIN, and TRNT1.
Accordingly, the patients reported herein exhibit typical HA20 phenotypic features: early-onset, recurrent fever, articular symptoms, recurrent oral, genital and/or gastrointestinal manifestations.

segregation.statement: Three affected carriers (father I.1, daughters II.1 and II.2) and one unaffected non-carrier (healthy mother I.2), all by Sanger sequencing. No unaffected carriers are reported.

quotes.quote: Sanger sequencing confirmed the TNFAIP3 c.707T>C, p.(Leu236Pro) variation in the proband and identified this variation in the related affected individuals (I.1 and II.1) (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
Lower panel – electropherograms from Sanger sequencing showing the heterozygous c.707T>C, p.(Leu236Pro) variation in individual II.2 but not in her healthy mother (individual I.2).

de_novo.statement: Not de novo: inherited from the affected father (I.1). The father's parents are not reported as tested.

quotes.quote: Sanger sequencing confirmed the TNFAIP3 c.707T>C, p.(Leu236Pro) variation in the proband and identified this variation in the related affected individuals (I.1 and II.1) (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).

functional.statement: Patient cells: reduced A20 protein in PBMCs of all three carriers vs two healthy individuals. Constructs in HEK293T: steady-state level 47.6% of WT; half-life 2.8 h vs WT stable at 24 h; MG132 restores the level to 91.3% of WT; reduced suppression of TNFα-induced NF-κB reporter activity vs WT at 25 and 50 ng; increased TRAF6 K63-ubiquitin smear (reduced deubiquitinase activity); GFP flow-cytometry assay with MG132 shows increased fluorescence, with Leu277* as positive and Phe127Cys as negative control.

quotes.quote: In contrast to two healthy individuals, all three patients (individuals I.1, II.1, and II.2) exhibited a significant reduction of A20 expression levels (Figure 3A).
As shown in Figure 3B, the steady-state protein amounts of A20_Leu236Pro were only 47.6% of that of the WT protein (0.54 for A20_WT vs 0.26 for A20_Leu236Pro).

Quantification of protein amounts at different time points showed that the half-life of A20_Leu236Pro was 2.8 hr, whereas the A20_WT protein was still highly expressed even after 24 hr of treatment (Figure 3C).
As shown in Figure 3D, substantial accumulation of A20_Leu236Pro was observed upon inhibition of the proteasome up to 91.3% of the WT protein levels (2.52 for A20_WT vs 2.30 for A20_Leu236Pro).

A20_Leu236Pro failed to suppress TNFα-induced NF-κB activity up to the levels of the WT counterpart: at 25 ng, A20_Leu236Pro decreased the NF-κB activity only by two folds compared to the empty vector.

This co-immunoprecipitation experiment revealed an increased intensity of the high molecular weight ubiquitin aggregate smear of TRAF6 in the presence of A20_Leu236Pro compared to the WT condition, thus indicating an altered DUB activity of A20_Leu236Pro (Figure 3F).

Fluorescence intensity increased for A20_Leu236Pro, A20_Leu275Pro and the positive control A20_Leu277*, indicating that like Leu236Pro, the Leu275Pro variant exhibits enhanced proteasomal degradation (curve shifted to the right in Figure 4 upper panel and increased fluorescence intensity in Figure 4 lower panel).
As negative control, we chose the polymorphic variant p.(Phe127Cys) (allele frequency = 0.0617 in gnomAD).

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Missense substitution, p.(Leu236Pro), in the OTU domain (from the batch HGVS and the papers). The authors propose loss of function through enhanced proteasomal degradation plus reduced NF-κB inhibition and deubiquitinase activity.

quotes.quote: AbstractA20 haploinsufficiency (HA20) is an autoinflammatory disease caused by heterozygous loss-of-function variations in TNFAIP3, the gene encoding the A20 protein.
Herein, we identified a novel TNFAIP3 variation, p.(Leu236Pro), located in the A20 ovarian tumor (OTU) domain and demonstrated its pathogenicity.

Further findings supporting the pathogenic significance of the p.(Leu236Pro) variation include enhanced UPS-dependent degradation of the A20_Leu236Pro protein, which is most likely responsible for the HA20 observed in the patients’ PBMCs.

computational_predictions.statement: CADD 29.5; PremPS ΔΔG 1.820 kcal/mol (destabilising), Site Directed Mutator 1.860, MAESTRO 1.752; Leu236 invariant across species.

quotes.quote: According to the Combined Annotation-Dependent Depletion (CADD, https://cadd.gs.washington.edu/snv) tool, the c.707T>C, p.(Leu236Pro) variation displays a score of 29.5, predictive of a pathogenic variation.
The single variation Leu236Pro of A20 is expected to be destabilizing, as indicated by the positive value of 1.820 kcal/mol for the change of unfolding Gibbs free energy ΔΔG (Table 2).
Similar results were obtained using two other prediction tools: Site Directed Mutator (ΔΔG=1.860 kcal/mol) and MAESTRO (Multi AgEnt STability pRedictiOn) (ΔΔG=1.752 kcal/mol).

However, the affected leucine residue at position 236 (Leu236) is located in the OTU domain of A20 (Figure 1B) and is invariant across species (Figure 1C), thereby supporting a deleterious effect of this amino acid substitution.

As for the missense variations located in the OTU domain, the pathogenic significance is demonstrated for four of them: p.(Glu192Lys) (Kadowaki et al., 2021), p.(Leu236Pro) (reported in this study), p.(Cys243Tyr) (Shigemura et al., 2016), and p.(Leu275Pro) (Aslani et al., 2022) and, which all fulfill the ACMG criteria for pathogenicity (Richards et al., 2015).

concerns: Same person likely recorded twice: 41741169 states that its patient 16 belongs to the family described by El Khouri et al. (37342083). Patient 16 is female, onset 1.3 years, consanguinity present, diagnosed at 12, which matches proband II.2 (female, onset 15 months, consanguineous parents, aged 13) rather than II.1 (onset 5 years). The pipeline keeps them as separate identities (HA20-ID0752 and HA20-ID0250); count them once.

If patient 16 is II.2, the two reports differ on some features: 41741169 records arthralgia as absent and lymphadenopathy as present during follow-up, while 37342083 reports asymmetric oligoarthralgia and does not mention lymphadenopathy.
37342083 contradicts itself on the authors' classification (Results versus Table 2 and Discussion); see authors_classification.
Parents are consanguineous; recessive autoinflammatory genes on the panel were reported negative, but the full panel content for other dominant genes is not listed.
Transcript: both papers use NM_006290 (41741169: NM_006290.4); the batch uses NM_001270508.2. Positions as written agree with the batch prediction (protein_check: agrees).
notes_for_panel: The best-documented candidate in this batch: segregation in three affected carriers with one non-carrier parent, patient-cell and construct assays with controls, and in-silico data, all from 37342083. 41741169 re-reports one family member.
